name: BenchBench-Cloning: Evaluating Molecular Cloning Design and Protocol Development (arXiv:2610.33355v1)
description: Preprint introducing BenchBench-Cloning, a 65-task molecular cloning benchmark, and reporting eight language-model agent systems scored on it at three reasoning settings each.

attributes.access_note: The construct-design tasks, graders and reference solutions are said in footnote 1 (page 3) to be available at https://github.com/benchling/benchbench-cloning. That URL returned HTTP 404 from both the web page and the GitHub API on 2026-11-06 at 2026-11-06T11:51:23Z, a repository search for 'benchbench-cloning' returned no results, and the repository is absent from benchling's public repositories. No code or data artifact was retrieved.
attributes.archive_note: The gzipped pdftotext -layout text layer of the pinned PDF is kept in the batch folder because every stored value was parsed from it. The PDF itself is refetchable at the versioned URL and is not archived; two downloads on 2026-11-06 were byte-identical.

evidence_concerns.message: Table D2's construct-design rate for Gemini 4 Argon at low effort, 31.9%, cannot be a mean of binary outcomes over the stated 15 tasks times 5 attempts: no integer numerator over 75 falls in its rounding window [23.8875, 23.9625], while all 23 other printed construct rates do. Its printed 95% interval [10.7, 52.0] is also byte-identical to the same system's top-effort interval. The two signals together indicate a transcription fault in the paper rather than a measured value, and the paper prints nothing that resolves it: the lane's aggregate is 15.8 under either 31.9 or 32.0, and Table G2's per-task solves are top-effort only. The printed value is kept as published and this entry withholds it from automatic comparison; the lane's other results are not covered.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Table D2, row 'Gemini 4 Argon' tier 'low' effort 'low', column 'Construct design % [95% CI]'

limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed. The benchmark is published by Benchling with DNAForge, and the authors both built the benchmark and ran every system on it.

Scores come from a cloning simulator and retrospective graders, not from constructs built at the bench; the authors state the simulator cannot capture every source of variation in reagents, handling, growth or reaction outcomes (Section 6.2).

Ten of the fifteen construct-design tasks are graded in part by GPT-6 Astra as a rubric judge, which is also one of the eight evaluated systems; the authors record occasional grading inconsistency as a limitation (Section 6.2).
The simulator reports only the first blocking error, so the failure categories in Tables E1 and E2 do not establish whether later steps would have succeeded (Section 6.2).
Single-turn: the authors state the format does not reflect the multi-turn way scientists work with a model (Section 6.2).

The construct-design tasks, graders and reference solutions are said in footnote 1 (page 3) to be available at https://github.com/benchling/benchbench-cloning. That URL returned HTTP 404 from both the web page and the GitHub API on 2026-11-06 at 2026-11-06T11:51:23Z, a repository search for 'benchbench-cloning' returned no results, and the repository is absent from benchling's public repositories. No code or data artifact was retrieved.

name: How good is AI at molecular biology? (Benchling announcement)
description: Benchling's announcement of the BenchBench-Cloning release, which gives the headline aggregate scores and situates the benchmark in the wider BenchBench suite.

evidence_concerns.message: The post says Kimi K3's 8.8% highlights "the gap between frontier and open-weight models at this task". The preprint's own Table 2 puts Gemini 3.8 Flash, a hosted frontier model, at 8.6%, below Kimi K3. The characterisation is not supported by the paper's ranking, so claims resting on the post's framing are withheld from comparison.

Table 3 lists NT v3 under phage-specific coverage (P) and Table 9 lists it as non-viral (N); Table 25 groups NTv3 rows under phage-specific coverage.

evidence_concerns.message: Table 25 prints one Macro-F1 per model for the taxonomy columns. For 143 of the 144 model-by-split taxonomy cells on the ALL-virus set, the printed value equals the mean of the five per-rank values in Table 26 rounded to two decimals. The exception is RNA-FM under the genus-disjoint split: Table 25 prints 48.67 and the mean of the Table 26 ranks (59.96, 65.35, 37.58, 58.78, 43.82) is 53.10. One of the two tables is wrong for that row, so RNA-FM ALL taxonomy G-Split should not be used in a comparison without checking the published code.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Table 25, row 'RNA-FM', column 'ALL viruses / Taxonomy / G-Split'; Table 26, row 'RNA-FM'

evidence_concerns.message: Table 3 lists NT v3 under phage-specific pretraining coverage (P) and Table 9 lists it as non-viral (N). Table 25 groups the NTv3 rows under phage-specific coverage, which is what the configurations record. Pretraining coverage is the paper's main explanatory variable, so NT v3 rows should not be used to support a coverage-versus-performance claim.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Table 3 row 'NT v3'; Table 9 row 'NT v3'; Table 25 section 'DNA Foundation Models (Phage-specific Coverage)'
